The Field Apothecary's Handbook

A brief practical compiled for town physicians, their apprentices, and any literate soul trusted near the medicine shelf.

I. Preparing Herbs

Fresh herbs may be crushed in a mortar with a pestle for 5 measures of their established extract. Spread them upon a drying rack first and a dried herb yields 10 measures and a stronger preparation. Drying takes about twenty minutes indoors, half that in open air, somewhat less beside a fire, and stops entirely beneath rain.

Two or more expressed herbal batches may be worked again with the pestle to make a concentrate. Half the mixture remains and only one effect is preserved. A journeyman may choose that effect; less-practised hands preserve the strongest presence. Herbs sharing an affinity strengthen the result.

An apprentice may bind one measure of essence before concentrating: Order steadies either medicine or poison, Life and Cycle reinforce beneficial preparations, and Poison reinforces harmful ones.

Established single-herb preparations

  • Artemisia: fortune and vitality tonic.
  • Atropa: weak nightshade poison. Harmful.
  • Benedictus: endurance and vigor tonic.
  • Calendula: mending salve.
  • Euphorbia: strengthening tonic.
  • Euphrasia: clarifying eye wash.
  • Hypericum: restorative clarity tonic.
  • Matricaria: sedating irritant. Harmful.
  • Mentha: cleansing clarity tea.
  • Paris: numbing poultice.
  • Rosa: soothing restorative.
  • Salvia: fortifying wisdom tonic.
  • Symphitum: mending tea.
  • Taraxacum: cleansing restorative.
  • Urtica: blood-restoring brew.
  • Valeriana: soothing sleep draught.

II. Remedies of the Heated Pot

Unless noted otherwise, begin with 20 measures of water in a cooking pot and warm it to 350 degrees. Optional dusts and herbs may be included where a formula permits them.

  • Symphitum Tea: 2 symphitum.
  • Taraxacum Extract: 3 taraxacum.
  • Urtica Brew: 2 urtica; iron dust is optional.
  • Hypericum Tonic: 2 hypericum; gold dust is optional.
  • Mentha Tea: 2 mentha.
  • Salvia Wisdom Tea: 2 salvia; bone meal is optional.
  • Artemisia Fortune Tea: 2 artemisia; silver dust is optional.
  • Euphorbia Strength Tea: 2 euphorbia; iron dust is optional.
  • Diluted Atropa Extract: 1 atropa. Poison.
  • Matricaria Irritant: 2 matricaria. Poison.
  • Rosa Water: 3 rosa, with no other solid ingredients in the pot.
  • Euphrasia Eye Wash: 2 euphrasia.
  • Valeriana Sleep Draught: 2 valeriana and 1 mentha.
  • Benedictus Vigor Tea: 2 benedictus; iron dust is optional.

Salves instead begin with 20 measures of strong alcohol and are warmed to 320 degrees: Calendula Salve takes 3 calendula; Paris Numbing Poultice takes 2 paris and 1 calendula.

Compound remedies

  • Herbalist's Panacea: 1 symphitum, 1 calendula, 1 urtica; rosa is optional.
  • Mercy Draught: 1 symphitum, 1 hypericum, 1 rosa, 1 silver dust, and 1 gold dust.
  • Witch's Bane: 2 rosa and 1 hypericum; silver dust is optional.
  • Scholar's Focus: 1 mentha, 1 euphrasia, and 1 salvia.
  • Moonwater Elixir: 1 artemisia and 1 hypericum; silver and water dusts are optional. Warm only to 320 degrees.
  • Warrior's Battle Broth: 1 benedictus, 1 valeriana, and 1 urtica; iron dust is optional.
  • Alchemist's Insight: 1 salvia and 1 mentha, alone in the pot; gold dust is optional.
  • Purification Draught: 1 rosa, 1 calendula, and 1 hypericum; silver and water dusts are optional.

III. Oils and Aromatic Candles

At 300 degrees, infuse 30 measures of strong alcohol with either 3 rosa for Rosa Perfume Oil, or 2 mentha and 1 euphrasia for Mentha Cooling Oil. An unlit common candle may be dressed with 5 measures of either oil. The resulting aromatic candle gently shares its beneficial effect with those standing close to its flame.

IV. Refined Medicines and Restricted Draughts

These exact formulae yield ten measures. Extra solvent does not increase the yield. Only a hand of the stated alchemical rank can keep the refinement stable.

  • Black Draught — apprentice, 300 degrees: 25 water, 1 wood charcoal, and 1 salt. Treats mild poisoning but draws other medicines and drugs from the blood as readily as toxins.
  • Blush — journeyman, 320 degrees: 10 measures diluted atropa, 10 matricaria irritant, and 5 rosa water. The resulting Fool's Blush smothers reason; excess harms the brain.
  • Grave Dream — expert, 320 degrees: 10 salvia wisdom tonic, 5 diluted atropa, 10 strong alcohol, and 2 capillus corpse caps. A violent hallucinogen; excess harms the brain.
  • Moonlily — expert, 330 degrees: 5 ozium, 5 pure moondust, and 5 strong alcohol. Numbs pain and lends endurance, but is fiercely habit-forming and excess strains the heart.
  • Nightshade Mercy — expert, 310 degrees: 20 diluted atropa, 10 strong alcohol, and 1 salt. A measured rescue tincture for failing breath and circulation, not ordinary wound care.

V. Essence-Cauldron Tonics

Both formulae require a journeyman and yield ten measures.

  • Pregnancy Potion: 4 Life, 3 Cycle, and 2 Water essence. The resulting Pregnancy Potion grants a brief season of certain fertility to the recipient, but cannot overcome an unwilling or incapable body.
  • Vertil: 4 Life, 2 Energia, and 2 Motion essence. The resulting Vertil grants a brief season of certain virility to the donor under the same natural limits.

VI. Salt and Charcoal

  • Salt: boil 25 measures of salt water in a cooking pot at 300 degrees for thirty seconds. One pile remains.
  • Wood Charcoal: roast one small log in a lit oven for one minute.

Final caution: label every vessel. Charcoal purges helpful substances, atropa and matricaria are poisons, and a pleasing name does not make a draught safe.
